name: Craig Jones Octopus Guard System
description: Explore Craig Jones Octopus Guard System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Craig Jones Octopus Guard System is a study framework for turning a half-guard exchange into a sweep, back exposure, or a controlled return to the feet.
overview:
Pressure passing can leave a guard player choosing between staying pinned and entering a scramble they do not understand. This guide examines an over-the-back connection as a way to organise that decision. Craig Jones's Octopus Guard 2.0 is the selected no-gi companion because its syllabus develops crossface problems, reversals, headlock responses and turtle continuations. Start with one half-guard situation before exploring the later branches.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: The remaining leg connection and upper-body freedom change which entry or recovery is available.
It can prevent the upper-body turn needed for the overback connection, so address that pressure before forcing the reach.
Check whether the post creates back exposure, preserves a sweep route, or requires a return to guard.
You still need a connection that survives the partner turning, disengaging, or standing.
The neck-control problem becomes immediate; stop chasing the original sweep and study the appropriate defensive response.
A repeatable half-guard start, one agreed response, and a clear endpoint such as top control or a recovered guard.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Reaching before freeing the upper body
common_obstacles.solution: Return to the crossface problem and identify the contact blocking the turn.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Calling every side pin octopus guard
common_obstacles.solution: Name what is still trapped and what has already been passed before choosing the next drill.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Chasing a back take after losing contact
common_obstacles.solution: Recover a familiar guard or stop at the lost connection before adding another attack.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Treating provocative lesson titles as technical guarantees
common_obstacles.solution: Judge the option against the partner response and study the detailed demonstration.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Half Guard and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.

products.title: Octopus Guard 2.0
products.blurb: A directly matched instructional companion for turning a half-guard exchange into a sweep, back exposure, or a controlled return to the feet. Review its published contents and sample to judge the teaching approach.
products.best_for: No-gi half-guard players who want an overback route into reversals and scrambles; readers seeking a gi-specific treatment can compare the Eduardo Telles guide.
products.study_focus: Begin with half guard versus side control and the crossface discussion; then compare the sweeping material with the later headlock and turtle sections.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: begin with 'Recognise the starting pin' from Half Guard. Record which partner response interrupts the plan and revisit that lesson before adding another branch.
